newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TAKING TOUGH STAND ON TAX EVASION.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TAKING TOUGH STAND ON TAX EVASION.

text.p: Tough action was being taken to deal with the growing incidence of tax fraud, Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said on Tuesday.
Speaking during the debate on two tax bills that implement changes announced in the March budget, Marcus said she wanted the swift prosecution and heavy sentencing of all found guilty of tax fraud.
"What is absolutely clear is that there is a declining morality around tax and tax payments, and we need to reinforce the need to pay tax," she said.
For example, she said, one firm appeared to have set out to create an establishment in order to commit fraud and to have colluded with clients to evade tax and VAT in fraud worth millions of rands.
"It is this kind of fraud that has to be dealt with and dealt with severely, and it is something that should not get off lightly," she said.
There was also fraud within the South African Revenue Services (SARS).
"SARS has a commitment to ensure that if fraud is found in its ranks, there will be prosecution and equally we want that prosecution to be swift and the sentences to be heavy," she said.
She agreed that it would do no good if the state just continually reacted to efforts to evade tax by coming up with counter-measures.

Marcus said that the legislation providing for SARS should be tabled in parliament on Wednesday or Thursday but warned that its promised administrative autonomy would not be a panacea to tax evasion on its own.
"We need to have effective systems in place and an effective team in SARS and ensure that the systems are enforceable," she said.
The recent tax amnesty had been only partially successful but had managed to get 147,000 people who had not been in the tax system onto the state's books, Marcus said.
